chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do a special thing for those who died from the Banu Hashim that he did not do for anyone else among the Muslims.
When he prayed over the Hashimi and sprinkled his grave with water, he would place his palm on the grave until his fingers were seen in the clay.

So the stranger would arrive or the traveler from the people of Medina, and he would see upon the new grave the mark of the palm of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he would say, 'One from the family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) has died.'

key_terms.الْهَاشِمِيِّ: The Hashimi (a member of the Banu Hashim clan)
key_terms.بَنِي هَاشِمٍ: Banu Hashim (the clan of Hashim, to which the Prophet belonged)

ai.seo_question: What special burial practice did the Prophet perform for the Banu Hashim clan?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the unique honor (*khasiyya*) bestowed upon the Banu Hashim, illustrating the Prophet’s personal affection and the distinct status of the Ahl al-Bayt within the early Muslim community. The physical mark left in the clay served not only as a practical identifier for travelers but also as a tangible sign of the Prophet’s enduring connection to his lineage, reinforcing the theological importance of the Prophet's family in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, 
from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to do a special thing with the one who died from the Clan of Hashim than with anyone from the Muslims.
When hesaww prayed Salaat upon the Hashimy and sprinkle his grave with the water, would place hissaww hand upon the grave until hissaww fingers would be seen to be in the clay.

Thus, if the stranger or a traveler from the people of Medina would come over, he would see upon the new grave the impact of the palm of Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and he would be saying, ‘The one from the family of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> has died’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah from who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The Messenger of Allah would do something over the grave of the people from the tribe of banu Hashim and he would not do on other Muslims’ graves.
After performing Salah (prayer) for a deceased from banu Hashim, sprinkling water over his grave, he would place his hand over the grave while his fingers pressed in the clay.

Strangers or travelers who came in the town and saw a new grave with marks of the fingers of the Messenger of Allah on it could tell that someone from banu Hashim has died. They would ask, ‘Who from the family of Muhammad, O Allah grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has died?”’
